sh-01.why: A Lewis Hamilton-themed pop-up with a wide range of merchandise: spend ¥99 to receive a complimentary coffee, and there are do-it-yourself activities.
sh-01.address: CITIC Square, 1168 Nanjing West Road, Jing'an District

sh-02.why: An Audi show-car display on Nanjing West Road, opposite the Louis Vuitton “Louis” store and facing the Starbucks.
sh-02.address: Nanjing West Road (opposite the Louis Vuitton “Louis” store), Huangpu District

sh-03.why: A PUMA pop-up next to the Red Bull one on Nanjing East Road, with racing simulators and a tyre-change game; finish the game and receive a free Red Bull.

sh-04.why: An Adidas Mercedes-AMG activation with a large George Russell screen at the No.1 Department Store on Nanjing East Road.
sh-04.address: No.1 Department Store, Nanjing East Road, Huangpu District

sh-05.why: The official Formula 1 merchandise store at West Bund Dream Center.
sh-05.address: West Bund Dream Center, Xuhui District

sh-06.why: A Bburago die-cast model pop-up in the L1 atrium of CP Jing'an, Jing'an District.
sh-06.address: CP Jing'an L1 atrium, Jing'an District

sh-07.why: HAUS NOWHERE at 798–802 Huaihai Middle Road, a retail concept space that includes Gentle Monster.

sh-08.why: ESCALIER at 685-1 Changle Road, Xuhui District — an F1 race-week installation.

sh-09.why: A TROPHY MARKET poster installation at 774 Changle Road, Jing'an District.

sh-10.why: A COSMOS RETRO FLOWER SHOP poster installation at 247 Fumin Road, Jing'an District.

sh-circuit.why: Home of the Formula 1 Chinese Grand Prix. The 15 March race is the P0 anchor, and the rest of the day is arranged around it.
sh-circuit.hours: Open per the race schedule on event days

sh-bund.why: Shanghai's classic waterfront promenade: the colonial-era Bund buildings on one side, the Lujiazui skyline on the other.

sh-yuyuan.why: A Ming-dynasty classical garden and the surrounding old-city bazaar.

sh-pearl.why: The landmark TV tower in Lujiazui, with a glass sightseeing deck over the Huangpu River.

sh-museum.why: The city's main museum of ancient Chinese art on People's Square, best known for bronzes and painting.

sh-xintiandi.why: Restored shikumen lanes turned into a dining and shopping district.

sh-wukang.why: The 1924 flat-iron apartment block at Wukang Road — the most photographed corner of the former French Concession.

sh-nanjingrd.why: China's best-known shopping street, running from People's Square down to the Bund.

sh-jingantemple.why: A gold-roofed Buddhist temple standing in the middle of the Jing'an business district.

sh-tower.why: China's tallest building, with the Top of Shanghai observation deck on the 118th floor.
sh-tower.address: 501 Yincheng Middle Road, Pudong New Area

sh-tianzifang.why: A warren of shikumen lanes packed with small studios, shops and cafés.
